purpose: Represent family, work, bereavement, rurality, mental-health, safeguarding, child-exposure and identity-development variables as time-ordered causal candidates without converting anecdotes or labels into causal conclusions.
privacy_rule: Do not store identifiable allegations, intimate identities, names, exact locations or unverified diagnoses from anecdotes. Convert examples into non-identifying abstract graph templates unless explicit, lawful, ethics-approved research data collection exists.

causal_edge_record_schema.promotion_rule: No edge is promoted from CANDIDATE_CAUSAL to CAUSAL_SUPPORTED_WITH_DESIGN from a single anecdote, cross-sectional association or temporal sequence alone.

abstract_example_template_from_user_scen.privacy: The user's anecdotal example is represented only as a synthetic topology; no names, exact place, allegation details or child identity are stored.

empirical_anchors.title: Rotation work in the resources sector: a systematic review of the impact on workers' families
empirical_anchors.finding: 19-study review: family mental-health impact remains unclear overall; partners may have more loneliness and poorer sleep when workers are away.
empirical_anchors.use: rotation-work family-context prior, not direct child causal coefficient

empirical_anchors.title: Work-family interface and children's mental health: a systematic review
empirical_anchors.finding: 25 studies; direct associations were mixed, while parental characteristics and parental mental health often acted as mediators.

empirical_anchors.title: Health impacts of parental migration on left-behind children and adolescents: a systematic review and meta-analysis
empirical_anchors.finding: 111 studies / 264,967 children; elevated risks for depression, anxiety and suicidal ideation among left-behind children, with substantial study-quality limitations and geographic concentration.
empirical_anchors.use: adjacent prolonged-parental-absence bridge only; not interchangeable with FIFO

empirical_anchors.title: Acquired Pedophilia: international Delphi-method-based consensus guidelines
empirical_anchors.finding: developmental etiology remains unknown and multifactorial; acquired cases are conceptually distinct and tied to underlying neurological disease.

empirical_anchors.title: Distinguishing Pedohebephebophilic Actors and Non-Actors: A Meta-Analysis
empirical_anchors.finding: 34 studies from 22 datasets distinguish actors from non-actors across multiple factors; cross-sectional evidence limits causal interpretation.
empirical_anchors.use: separates sexual interest from acting/offending and supports multivariable risk modeling

empirical_anchors.title: Ensuring Comprehensive Care and Support for Transgender and Gender-Diverse Children and Adolescents
empirical_anchors.finding: TGD identity is not itself a mental disorder; mental-health disparities are linked to multifactorial stressors including stigma, rejection and limited access to appropriate care; family acceptance/rejection affects well-being and disclosure more than identity determination.
empirical_anchors.use: forbids trauma-to-gender-identity causal shortcut and separates identity from mental-health outcomes

empirical_anchors.title: Workforce strategies to address children's mental health and behavioural needs in rural, regional and remote areas: A scoping review
empirical_anchors.finding: rural/remote children face barriers to mental-health service access.
empirical_anchors.use: rurality as access/context mediator rather than identity or diagnosis cause

analysis_plan: 1. Build within-family timeline before drawing arrows.
2. Mark each node by evidence provenance and uncertainty.
3. Separate preference/clinical state, offending behavior and child exposure.
4. Separate child mental-health outcomes from gender identity/self-description.
5. Enumerate competing DAGs before estimating any preferred path.
6. Test temporal precedence and dose/repetition where meaningful.
7. Match or adjust for confounders: socioeconomic status, substance use, baseline mental health, prior family conflict, prior sexual-interest history, service access, age and developmental stage.
8. Test mediators rather than assigning direct group effects.
9. Use negative controls and sibling/within-person/roster-phase designs where possible.
10. Promote only replicated edges with compatible measurement and independent samples.
topa_killer_tests: If the alleged cause occurred after the outcome began, kill the edge.
If the edge disappears after baseline-history adjustment, shift weight to preexisting state.
If rurality effect disappears after care-access and socioeconomic matching, remove rurality from causal interpretation.
If rotation-work effect disappears after parental mental-health and communication mediators, classify it as mediated rather than direct.
If gender identity predates the alleged trauma or persists independently of it, kill trauma-causes-identity hypothesis.
Even if trauma and TGD identity co-occur, do not infer causation without a validated developmental design; prioritize mental-health and support outcomes instead.
If offending occurs without evidence of paedophilic preference, do not diagnose paedophilic disorder from behavior alone.
If paedophilic preference exists without offending, do not label the person an offender.
claim_ceiling: This protocol can identify plausible causal pathways, mediators, confounders and falsified shortcuts. It cannot diagnose individuals or infer causation from an anecdotal family history.
seal: MAP THE CHAIN; DO NOT INVENT THE ARROW.
